content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working on a [product_name] Web Editor project for my home automation using [product_name] ([version_no]). When I use a flag as a variable for a writable input, everything operates correctly, but with network inputs, I am unable to control them. I can view the status of a network output but cannot write to a network input. Is there an extra configuration needed for network inputs? The addresses I’m using for inputs range from v1.1 to 1.6.

No additional settings are necessary, you only need to activate the "Writable" option. It seems there might be an overlap or double usage in the virtual memory. Could you upload your [product_name] Web Editor project and the corresponding [product_name] program?

Hello [user_name], Thank you for your response. I’ve attached a small section of the full program that isn’t working as intended. Connection to M1 functions correctly (I can control it via [product_name] Web Editor), but the network input cannot be controlled. Thanks in advance for your help.

Is this the entire program or just a part? This setup works without issues in my [product_name]. Assigning a flag in parallel with the network input is not recommended. If the flag is high, the network input can trigger the pulse relay.

Hello [user_name], This was only a section from a five-page program, used to see if I could add this feature. After creating a new [product_name] Web Editor project from the beginning, I can now control network inputs. I’m unsure what went wrong in the previous version, but I’m glad it’s now working. Thank you for your assistance.
In the future, please upload both the complete project and the full program.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced difficulties controlling network inputs via [product_name] Web Editor with [product_name] ([version_no]) in a home automation setup. While using flags as writable variables worked, network input control did not function, though network output status was visible. By starting a new project from scratch, network inputs could be controlled successfully, but the underlying reason for the earlier issue remained unidentified.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects reliable control of network inputs through [product_name] Web Editor, similar to flag variables, without needing undocumented settings or encountering memory allocation problems.
